clue.text: In bad shape, convict found in pile of waste

indicators.note: something in bad condition is knocked about, so the word after it is jumbled
one thing found inside another sits within it, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: the letters of shape rearranged
an old lag is a long-serving convict

explanation.surface: A prisoner in poor condition turns up lying on a rubbish dump.
explanation.walkthrough: An old lag is British slang for a long-serving convict. 'In bad shape' reads as one phrase about the prisoner, but 'In bad' is the signal and 'shape' the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A slag heap is a mound of mining or smelting refuse, literally a pile of waste material.

clue.text: Dash for whisky?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to put an end to, as in dashing someone's hopes
second meaning: whisky distilled in Scotland

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a splash of spirit in a glass; the verb sense of Dash (to ruin or thwart a plan or rumour) is the real first meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a plan is to quash it, and Scotch is the usual name for whisky made in Scotland.

clue.text: The cop arranged to host at-home for old Chilean general

indicators.note: things arranged are put into a fresh order, so those letters are reordered
a host takes a guest inside, so the rearranged letters surround the other piece

parts.note: the six letters of the cop rearranged
being at home is being in

explanation.surface: A police officer is organised to throw a house party for a former military dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At-home' looks like a noun for a party, which suits the surface, but it is read as the adverb meaning in.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusto Pinochet was the army general who ruled Chile as dictator from 1973 to 1990.

clue.text: The French rave about tadpoles, say

indicators.note: about can mean moving around in disorder, so the following word is scrambled

parts.note: la is the French feminine definite article
rave with its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: French people enthuse about frog spawn hatchlings.
explanation.definitionFit: Tadpoles are the immature stage of frogs, an example of the young forms called larvae, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Anarchists' leader occupying position in royal residence

indicators.note: to occupy a place is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a position is a place

indicators.note: the leader of a group goes in front, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: first letter of Anarchists'

explanation.surface: The head of a band of anarchists takes up a post inside the royal home.
explanation.definitionFit: A palace is the official home of a monarch, so it is a royal residence.

clue.text: With fake ring, marry at last

parts.note: to ring someone is to phone them

indicators.note: at last points to the end, so only the final letter is used

parts.note: last letter of marry

explanation.surface: Someone proposes marriage at long last, using a counterfeit engagement ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like the jewellery of the wedding scene, but it is the verb meaning to call on the telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoney is an informal adjective for something counterfeit or not genuine, a synonym of fake.

clue.text: Celebrated singer visits lake before start of Indian religious festival

parts.note: a diva is a famous female opera singer
L is the map abbreviation for lake

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: first letter of Indian

explanation.surface: A famous singer travels to a lake ahead of a Hindu celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' looks like part of the definition, but only its first letter is used; the definition is just the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Divali (also Diwali) is the Hindu, Sikh and Jain festival of lights held each autumn.

clue.text: State of former PM's heart?

indicators.note: the heart is what is left inside once the outer edges are trimmed away

parts.note: Benjamin Disraeli was a 19th-century British Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A question about what lay at the core of a past prime minister's thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first and last letters of DISRAELI to leave the country's name. The question mark admits the slightly loose phrasing.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel is a sovereign country in the Middle East, so it is a state.

clue.text: Author of Ale denied being drunk

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

parts.note: all eleven letters of these three words rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer refuses to admit he has been drinking beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' looks like a link between Author and Ale, but its letters belong to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe was the English novelist who wrote Robinson Crusoe and Moll Flanders.

clue.text: Don't remember to make time

parts.note: to forge is to make, as a smith does
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A reminder note about failing to find time for something.
explanation.definitionFit: To forget is to fail to recall something, so it means not to remember.

clue.text: Leave oar tangled in plant

indicators.note: things tangled are twisted out of order, so those letters are mixed up

parts.note: all eight letters of these words rearranged

explanation.surface: A rower abandons an oar snagged in weeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloe vera is a succulent species grown for the soothing gel in its leaves.

clue.text: Told to find out about present

indicators.note: something told is spoken, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: to hear of something is to find out about it

explanation.surface: Someone is instructed to discover what is going on now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift or the current time, but here it is the adjective meaning in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'here' at a roll call means you are in attendance, i.e. present.

clue.text: Raised empty hand containing 8 points

indicators.note: containing means holding something within, so the other pieces go inside
an empty word has lost its insides, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: outer letters of hand
the number written out
compass points: east, north, east

explanation.surface: A card player lifts a hand with nothing in it holding eight scoring points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' supplies three compass letters at once; bridge or whist players will first read it as card scores.
explanation.definitionFit: To heighten is to make higher, so heightened describes something lifted or increased.

clue.text: Unsocial pet may be a risky investment

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters could become something else when rearranged

parts.note: all eleven letters of these words rearranged

explanation.surface: Buying an antisocial animal could turn out to be a gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: Speculation is buying assets in the hope of quick profit while accepting high risk of loss.

clue.text: Chicken getting answer as well as parrot

parts.note: a cock is a male chicken
A is the abbreviation for answer
too means also, as well

explanation.surface: A chicken gets a reply, and so does a parrot.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockatoo is a crested bird of the parrot family from Australasia.

clue.text: Solo nerd translated medieval language

indicators.note: translating turns words into another form, so these letters are re-formed

parts.note: all eight letters of these words rearranged

explanation.surface: A lone geek renders an ancient tongue into English.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Norse was the Germanic tongue of the Vikings, spoken in Scandinavia in the Middle Ages.

clue.text: Father with part to play in prisoner's conditional release

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a part in a play is a role

explanation.surface: A dad has an acting role in a drama about an inmate's early freedom.
explanation.definitionFit: Parole is the early release of a prisoner on the condition of good behaviour.

clue.text: Voracious animals turning up in empty granary

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
an empty word has lost its middle, leaving just its first and last letters

parts.note: outer letters of granary

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means read from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: deer are animals

explanation.surface: Hungry creatures show up in a grain store that has been emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: Greedy and voracious both describe an insatiable appetite, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Carer stews exotic vegetable

indicators.note: exotic means strange or unusual, so the letters take an unfamiliar new order

parts.note: all ten letters of these words rearranged

explanation.surface: A care worker cooks an unusual vegetable dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stews' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; the signal is 'exotic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Watercress is a peppery leafy plant eaten as a salad green, so it counts as a vegetable.

clue.text: Amorous chap embraces occupational therapist

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap your arms around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a man's name standing for any chap
OT is the abbreviation for occupational therapist

explanation.surface: A lovestruck man hugs his therapist.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotic describes sexual desire or arousal, closely akin to amorous feeling.

clue.text: Was a candidate in examination given to anger in ironic composition?

parts.note: to sit an exam is to be a candidate in it
ire is anger

explanation.surface: An exam candidate grows angry while writing a sarcastic essay.
explanation.definitionFit: A satire is a piece of writing that mocks its target through irony and ridicule.

clue.text: Read revolutionary's challenge

indicators.note: a revolutionary overturns the established order, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: the four letters of read rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebel reads a provocation.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', linking wordplay to definition rather than showing possession.
explanation.definitionFit: A dare is a challenge to someone to do something bold or risky.

clue.text: Colonel taking gold to a function in US state

parts.note: COL is the abbreviation for Colonel
or is the heraldic word for gold
taken as written
a do is a party or social function

explanation.surface: An army officer brings gold to a party somewhere in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Colorado is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the Rocky Mountain region.

clue.text: With reimbursed cash, Elizabeth David originally decorated cover of book

indicators.note: read as re-imbursed: paid back, so the word goes back the way it came

parts.note: loot is slang for money

indicators.note: originally points to how each word begins, so only initial letters are taken

parts.note: first letters of Elizabeth and David

explanation.surface: Elizabeth David, the cookery writer, spends her refunded money on fancy bindings for her books.
explanation.walkthrough: Elizabeth David was a famous British cookery writer. The definition is an adjective phrase: 'decorated' qualifies the cover of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Tooled leather has patterns pressed or engraved into it, the traditional way of ornamenting a fine book binding.

clue.text: Editor is working with inventor

parts.note: ED is the abbreviation for editor
taken as written
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor collaborates with a famous inventor.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the American inventor behind the phonograph and a practical light bulb.

clue.text: Ill tempered Conservative showing signs of age?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
old metal shows its age by going rusty

explanation.surface: A grumpy old Tory politician is past his prime.
explanation.definitionFit: Crusty is used of people who are irritable and gruff, a synonym of bad-tempered.
